problem: CLIP-style contrastive vision-language representations give poor fine-grained scene understanding for embodied control, and control-specific representations (R3M, VC-1) transfer poorly across manipulation and navigation. Text-to-image diffusion models were unexplored as representations for control.
motivation: Diffusion models are trained to generate images from text, so their internal features should hold fine-grained, text-conditioned visuo-spatial information. Their cross-attention maps are category-agnostic and could help open-vocabulary generalization and interpretability.
key_idea: Extract frozen, text-conditioned multi-layer features (and cross-attention maps) from the Stable Diffusion U-Net on lightly noised observations as representations for downstream policies (Stable Control Representations, SCR).
insight: Multi-layer aggregation (Down[1-3]+Mid 49.9 vs Mid only 41.6 on Franka-Kitchen) and small noise timesteps matter most. Spatial aggregation via a conv compression layer also matters, and with it CLIP's fine-grained prediction jumps (Refer Exp. 68.1 to 94.3), so CLIP's control weakness is not due to missing spatial information. Text prompts to the U-Net help only when the task is language-conditioned; text-aligned attention maps help open-vocabulary OVMM (+1.7).
method: Feature extraction: encode the image with the SD VAE, noise the latent to timestep t, and run the U-Net with the text prompt; take the mid block and the last three down-block outputs.

Layer aggregation: bilinearly interpolate the maps to 8x8, concatenate channel-wise (102,400 dims), and reduce with a learnable conv compression layer before the policy; the same compression layer is used for all baselines.
Timestep selection: a fixed timestep per task, chosen by coarse grid search (0 for Franka-Kitchen/ImageNav, 100 for OVMM, 200 for Meta-World).

Prompting: the task text (e.g. target object category) is fed to the U-Net; for purely visual tasks the prompt is empty. For language tasks the CLIP text embedding is also concatenated to the features.
SCR-Attn: word-level cross-attention maps between visual features and CLIP text embeddings (following DAAM) are fused with the U-Net features, giving interpretable, category-agnostic cues.

SCR-FT: fine-tune the SD U-Net (VAE frozen) with the standard text-conditioned diffusion loss on 1.3M image-text pairs from EpicKitchens, SS-v2 and Bridge-v2 (1 epoch, 5k steps, 256x256, embodiment name prepended to the prompt), with no task data.
Downstream policies: frozen encoder plus a small MLP trained by behavior cloning for manipulation, or an LSTM trained with DD-PPO for navigation.

setting.backbone: Stable Diffusion v1.5 U-Net (frozen features; optionally fine-tuned on robotics videos) + CLIP text encoder; downstream MLP / LSTM policies trained from scratch
setting.model_size: ~400M parameters forward pass through SD (U-Net+VAE+text encoder)
setting.training_data: SD pre-trained on LAION-2B; SCR-FT fine-tuned on 1.3M image-text pairs from EpicKitchens, SS-v2, Bridge-v2; policies trained per task (25 demos for manipulation; 500M steps ImageNav, 100M steps OVMM RL)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (ImageNav 128x128; Gaze RGB-D camera with RGB used) plus proprioception for manipulation; CLIP text embedding of the target category for OVMM
setting.action_space: ImageNav: discrete MOVE_FORWARD 25cm / TURN 30° / STOP; OVMM Gaze: continuous forward 5-25cm, turn 5-30°, head pan/tilt, Pick; manipulation: continuous control
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson ImageNav, HSSD OVMM), Meta-World, RoboHive Franka-Kitchen
setting.privileged: none (only the 'Oracle' baseline uses GT object masks)

numbers.eval_set_note: 4200 episodes in 14 held-out Gibson scenes; note the dataset is Gibson, so the benchmark tag is approximate
numbers.extra: frozen encoder, LSTM policy DD-PPO 500M steps; Gibson scenes
fine-tuned on 1.3M robotics image-text pairs; the text says only the fine-tuned variant was run, but the table lists both SCR and SCR-FT

numbers.eval_set_note: 1199 validation episodes, 12 HSSD scenes, 106 seen and 22 unseen categories; modified harder Gaze sub-task only
numbers.extra: modified Gaze task with random start heading within 2.0m; 100M RL steps; LSTM initialized from the Oracle

numbers_note: ImageNav rows use Gibson scenes (4200 episodes) mapped to the closest canonical name. OVMM is a modified Gaze sub-task, not the full OVMM benchmark. The paper describes 'only SCR-FT run' for ImageNav, yet the table also gives SCR = 73.9.
results: SCR variants are competitive across manipulation and navigation. On the OVMM Gaze task SCR-FT-Attn gets 43.6 SR versus VC-1 40.6, CLIP 38.7 and Detic 36.7 (Oracle 77.6). On ImageNav SCR reaches 73.9 vs VC-1 70.3. SCR-FT has the best average normalized score (0.949) across four control benchmarks, while R3M wins few-shot manipulation but fails on navigation.
limitations: Requires a ~400M-parameter forward pass, and the timestep, prompt and layers must be tuned per task.
Fine-tuning on robotics data does not help consistently (e.g. ImageNav 73.9 to 69.5, and no gain on visual prediction), and a many-to-one text-video alignment problem exists.
Long text guidance is weakly captured by the U-Net, so the CLIP text embedding must still be concatenated; a large gap to the Oracle remains on OVMM.
builds_on: Diffusion-based representation extraction (Tian, Yang, Xu et al.)
